feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector/platform expertise. It is generally well written and polished, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused evidence beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility: long tenure at NACo, promotion history, and concrete platform scale signals like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”  
- Broad, relevant skill mix: combines strategy, governance, analytics, CMS/platform delivery, and multimedia in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than impact. Include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and readability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation and bullet formatting vary; “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—consider “French (A2, improving).” Also standardize title casing (e.g., “Coleman Davis” vs “DAVIS”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and NACo experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning line, e.g. “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years in public-sector and advocacy organizations.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience to increase impact, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: “Leads web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial operations, multimedia, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider revised version: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years building enterprise web, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads modernization across Drupal platforms, analytics, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies/footer; “AI-enabled search” is more specific and better supported.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as broader, executive-level competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and systems integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of mixing “&” with other constructions for a cleaner, more formal tone.
- Consider replacing “editorial systems” with “content operations” to align more directly with the experience section.
- If space is tight, shorten “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also repeated in Technical + IT and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce your current positioning, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a short, punchy accomplishment rather than a full sentence.
- Tighten wording: “AI-enabled” appears repeatedly; vary language and remove filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure, e.g., start each item with a strong verb and keep each to one line.
- Consider this rewrite:  
  AI Hybrid Search — Built a legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.  
  We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, storytelling modules, and downloadable resources.  
  Organization Anniversary Campaign — Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and an interactive conference display.  
  Advocacy Video Series — Launched a recurring advocacy video program across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video work closely overlap with current and NACo experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs if this section stays.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and add 1–2 concrete outcomes or scale indicators to make the impact clearer.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes-focused phrasing: “Designed organization-wide workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Combine overlapping web/CMS bullets into one stronger bullet: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Add measurable context where possible: number of sites/pages/users, reduction in publishing time, improved search success, adoption across teams, or performance gains from the AI-enabled search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the NACo Director role; keep this entry focused on what is new here, especially AI-enabled search and current consulting scope.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections; emphasize business impact, not tool execution alone.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale indicators. It should be tightened to emphasize transformation outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific or measurable: add email open/click improvements, audience growth, campaign results, or production volume if available; otherwise shorten this bullet.
- Tighten operations language: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video/programming language also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize studio build-out and organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned at this level: channel operations, editorial coordination, and repeatable advocacy content.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to clarify scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, supporting organization-wide editorial planning and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the format rather than originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and more outcome-oriented by emphasizing enterprise scope and governance leadership.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with tighter, higher-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “content strategy” to sound more senior and distinct from execution-level work.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale already proven in recent roles: 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers.
- Keep terminology consistent with recent experience: use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” if that’s your preferred phrasing across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Make it more outcome-oriented and selective, emphasizing recent strengths from the 2022–present roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • SharePoint & Power Pages • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search”
- Put the strongest/recent differentiators first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, and AI-enabled search; these are most supported by current and recent experience.
- Cut lower-value filler if space is tight; consider dropping either WordPress or jQuery unless they are important for target roles.
- If possible, add light specificity elsewhere in the CV rather than here, e.g., “Drupal migration for 10,000+ pages” or “AI-enabled search initiative,” since skills sections work best when concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT” (Web Platforms & CMS; Coding & Technical Implementation; Automation & Workflow Systems).
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and recent experience bullets.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns well with the 2022–present leadership work, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing decision-making impact will make it stronger.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platforms-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than just listing tools.
- Use grouped phrasing for concision: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace weaker items like “Leadership reporting” with more specific business language: “executive dashboards,” “KPI framework design,” or “performance reporting for leadership”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and performance reporting • SEO and user behavior analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- Tool names here overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry, so this section should stay concise and outcome-focused rather than restating the same accomplishment.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads as a generic tool list rather than a senior, outcomes-oriented capability statement. It should better reflect recent leadership-level multimedia work and align with the “broadcast-quality in-house studio” achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability + scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider adding a leadership/strategy angle to match recent roles: “Multimedia production strategy” or “Studio buildout and operations”
- Replace “video production and editing” with a tighter, more senior phrase like “Video production, editing, and distribution” only if distribution isn’t covered elsewhere
- If space allows, make it more distinctive: “Broadcast-quality studio production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera systems • Virtual event operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording here to avoid repetition.
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the NACo studio bullet; keep this skills item concise and non-narrative.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, lead with that and trim lower-signal items.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” → put Drupal first and consider dropping GitHub Pages unless used professionally.
- If space allows, add level/context instead of just names: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages.”
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid adding CMS modernization or technical implementation terms already covered elsewhere.
- If you want stronger impact, rename to “CMS & Web Platforms” and align with recent experience emphasis on Drupal-led modernization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus related capabilities.
- “Web & CMS administration” in Core Competencies also covers similar ground; consider consolidating to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools tied to recent work and trimming older/basic items.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to highlight applied technical execution, e.g. “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for clarity: “Integrations & tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager”
- Keep newer/distinctive tools prominent: “Serverless & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or depth markers instead of version numbers/basic labels, e.g. replace “HTML5 • CSS3” with “semantic HTML • responsive CSS” or note “custom front-end troubleshooting”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations.”
- Consider removing jQuery if it is not central to recent work, since newer experience emphasizes CMS modernization, AI search, and workflow systems.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Tighten to the strongest, most relevant tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Drop older/lower-signal items unless central to recent work: Basecamp, Trello.
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar category tools; listing all four can look padded unless each was used meaningfully in recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare to show level of use or strategic value. Since recent roles emphasize email leadership, this should signal platform administration/automation rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, Journeys & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign operations, segmentation, automated journeys, newsletter distribution)
- If accurate, prioritize by strongest/recent platform first; e.g., Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp
- If one platform was central in the 2022–2024 director role, consider adding proficiency context elsewhere instead of here: “led email communications for newsletters reaching tens of thousands”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” in this skills line if it already appears in NACo experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader digital strategy language elsewhere; keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” It also mixes platforms with capabilities, making it read less crisply than your stronger recent experience suggests.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Tighten content to: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console
- Move capabilities out of this line item: replace SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding with a separate skills line elsewhere only if not already covered as “KPI design • Leadership reporting • SEO and performance analysis”
- If you want stronger impact alignment, order by demonstrated recent use: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Power BI • Looker Studio • BigQuery • Google Search Console

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping detail in one place and shortening the other.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with Looker Studio/Power BI and with “reporting infrastructure” language in Core Competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and distinct as the foundation-building phase of your digital leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social media and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Tighten the management reference: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume, audience growth, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; frame this as establishing initial processes rather than broader operational leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes/ownership, while avoiding overlap with later multimedia-heavy NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer action, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audiences served, teams supported, or specific projects/policy areas.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on innovation/research support + first podcast.
- Avoid repeating broad “supporting organizational programs and policy work” language used elsewhere unless you can specify the function or result.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Make it more tool-specific and concise, reserving production scope/impact for recent roles.

Suggested edit:
